articles.body: Ram Charan and director Sukumar have officially begun their much-awaited second collaboration, tentatively titled ‘RC17’. The makers are expected to announce the remaining cast and crew details in the coming days.Ram Charan and Sukumar reunite after ‘Rangasthalam’‘RC17’ was officially announced in March 2024, when Ram Charan shared a picture with Sukumar during Holi. articles.title: Australian Influencer’s Bali Vacation Ends in ICU After Headache Turns Out to Be Meningitis
articles.summary: Australian fitness influencer woke up with a bad headache in Bali but has spent over a week in a hospital intensive care unit due to meningitis. Meningitis i...
articles.body:
Australian fitness influencer woke up with a bad headache in Bali but has spent over a week in a hospital intensive care unit due to meningitis. Meningitis is an infection of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord and can be fatal if not treated quickly.

Khiana Smith, 23, a fitness creator and online coach from Gold Coast, Australia, told news.com.au that she had been in intensive care for eight days with bacterial and viral meningitis, pneumonia she got in the hospital, and fluid in her lungs, according to the New York Post .

"I just woke up one day, and I had the worst headache," Smith said.

Smith runs Her Method, a fitness and nutrition coaching business, and has been posting updates from her hospital bed to TikTok and Instagram, where she has nearly 87,000 followers combined, TMZ reported.

Smith had been traveling in Europe for two weeks and had been in Bali for about a week when she fell ill, the Post reported. The headache quickly turned into severe head pain, dizziness, slurred speech, blurred vision, and extreme sensitivity to light, UNILAD reported , citing her posts.

IV drip treatment she had at the villa did not improve her symptoms, and a doctor who checked her called an ambulance, which took her to a hospital within minutes. Within a few hours, she had a CT scan and intravenous antibiotics, a quick response that her mother said probably saved her life.

Doctors do not yet know how she was infected. Possible sources include contaminated food, water she swam in, or another passenger on a flight.

Her stories have slight discrepancies. Smith told news.com.au she had been in intensive care for eight days, while TMZ said nine. The infection has left her with memory problems and difficulties following conversations.

"I really struggle to remember things," Smith said in a TikTok video.

She also had to deal with language barriers as she tried to understand her condition, UNILAD reported. In her latest update, Smith said she felt a bit better after getting out of bed and walking for the first time in more than a week.

Her mother, Cass Smith, flew to Indonesia as soon as she found out her daughter was ill. She told news.com.au that nothing is scarier than knowing her child is struggling for her life in another country, thousands of kilometers from home, the Post reported.

The family commended Indonesian medical staff despite the language barrier. When her condition deteriorated, doctors were able to reach Smith within 10 to 15 minutes, a level of care the family said is more than they usually get in Australian hospitals.

Travel insurance is covering her hospital bills. Cass Smith said she warned her daughter to buy a policy before the trip and advised other travelers to do the same.

Smith has not been cleared to fly back home due to swelling in her brain and concerns about cabin pressure. The family hopes doctors will give her clearance in about a week, when she plans to cut her trip short and recover on the Gold Coast. They also hope the quick start of antibiotics will prevent any long-term consequences and that her memory loss will be temporary.

Hundreds of followers have sent her messages of support. Smith, who says she eats healthy and exercises every day, has used her posts to warn others that serious illness can happen to anyone.

"Don't take your life or health for granted ever," she told her followers, according to UNILAD.

Meningitis is swelling of the protective lining of the brain and spinal cord. Bacterial meningitis is a serious illness and can kill in a few hours, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says. Most people recover with proper care, but survivors may suffer permanent disabilities, and complications can include seizures, coma, and even death. Doctors treat it with antibiotics, which the CDC says should start as soon as possible.

Viral meningitis is the most common type and is less serious. Most people recover from mild cases on their own within seven to 10 days, though severe cases may require hospitalization, the CDC says.

Bali has a reputation for having bacterial meningitis. A 2019 study in Emerging Infectious Diseases , a CDC journal, found that 44 of 71 cases of acute bacterial meningitis treated at Denpasar's main hospital from 2014 to 2017 were caused by Streptococcus suis, a bacterium carried by pigs. Researchers attributed those infections primarily to handling pigs and eating raw pork products, including traditional dishes made from fresh pig blood. About 11% of the patients in the study died.

No particular cause has been announced in Smith's case.

Its India gross collection has reached Rs 451.94 crore, while the worldwide gross stands at Rs 584.74 crore.The film's latest figures further strengthen its position as one of the biggest commercial successes in the franchise.The thriller maintained its hold across theatres on Sunday, recording collections from 3,089 shows. Its domestic performance also showed a slight improvement compared to the previous day. Meanwhile, the film's overseas business continued to contribute significantly to its overall earnings.'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' Day 31 box office collectionAccording to Sacnilk, 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' collected Rs 1.75 crore in India net earnings on Sunday, November 1. This represents a 9.4% increase over its previous day's collection of Rs 1.60 crore. The film collected Rs 4.35 crore in India net earnings during the three-day weekend ending November 1. Sunday contributed the highest share, with the thriller registering a better collection than the previous day.The film's overseas performance also added to its impressive worldwide total. It earned Rs 25 lakh from international markets on Day 31, taking its cumulative overseas gross collection to Rs 132.80 crore. With its domestic and international earnings combined, the Ajay Devgn starrer has reached a worldwide gross collection of Rs 584.74 crore.'Drishyam 3' week-wise performanceIts opening week remains the biggest contributor to its domestic earnings. 'Drishyam 2' reportedly had a production budget of Rs 90 crore, while an additional Rs 60 crore was spent on salaries. The original 'Drishyam' was reportedly made on a budget of Rs 65 crore. The latest instalment's box office performance marks a significant commercial achievement for the franchise.'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' plot: Vijay Salgaonkar faces a new investigationThe story follows Vijay Salgaonkar years after he successfully managed to evade the law. However, his past continues to haunt him as Meera Deshmukh returns with a different objective. Rather than pursuing justice through conventional means, she seeks revenge. articles.title: Andrew Shue marries Marilee Fiebig, weeks after their exes Amy Robach and T.J. Holmes tied the knot
articles.summary: The couple’s “low-key” ceremony was held at their 92-acre New Jersey estate on Sunday.
articles.body:
Andrew Shue and Marilee Fiebig have tied the knot after three years of dating.

The Melrose Place star and immigration attorney wed in a "low-key" ceremony at their 92-acre New Jersey estate on Sunday.

Shue and Fiebig bonded after their respective former spouses, Good Morning America anchors Amy Robach and T.J. Holmes, went public with their relationship in 2022.

Andrew Shue and Marilee Fiebig are officially married!

The Melrose Place alum and the immigration attorney tied the knot on Sunday in a "low-key" ceremony at their 92-acre estate outside of Stockton, N.J., confirms Entertainment Weekly 's sister site PEOPLE . The Daily Mail also published photos of Fiebig in her white lace wedding gown.

The nuptials come just days after news broke that Shue and Fiebig were engaged . The couple famously bonded after their former spouses, Good Morning America anchors Amy Robach and T.J. Holmes, were romantically linked .

Robach and Holmes, meanwhile, got married last month in Arkansas.

"We're very grateful and hopeful," Shue told PEOPLE last week about his engagement to Fiebig. "I don't know how it happened, but there's a happy ending."

The photographs of the wedding show Sabine, Fiebig's 13-year-old daughter with Holmes, serving as one of her bridesmaids alongside the attorney's close friend, finance executive Lisa Bashishow. The groom's sister, Oscar-nominated Leaving Las Vegas actress Elisabeth Shue, also attended the ceremony.

Entertainment Weekly has reached out to representatives for Shue and Fiebig for comment.

Shue and Fiebig, coincidentally, were both married to their previous spouses from 2010 to 2023. Fiebig and Holmes share Sabine, while Shue did not have any children with Robach.

"Relationships are hard. They're messy. They're not perfect. We have fought for love, and I can say I have never been happier. I am with my best friend," Robach said in December 2023, a year after her relationship with Holmes came to light, resulting in the couple's exit from GMA .

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

"Marilee's sole focus has remained on the overall best interest of her 9-year-old daughter," an attorney for Fiebig said at the time .

For his part, Shue reflected on how the end of his marriage to Robach led to him finding "The One."

"I had to accept my own part in marriage not working out for me and in not understanding myself well enough and not understanding what matters in a relationship well enough to find the right person for me, and that has been an extraordinary gift," he told PEOPLE . "I don't know how it happened, but I can say I'm grateful."

articles.title: Amitabh Bachchan pays emotional tribute to Sanjay Gupta: ‘Companions from the world of art are being snatched away’
articles.summary: Sanjay Gupta, the filmmaker who gave audiences 'Kaante', 'Kaabil' and 'Shootout at Wadala', passed away on October 30 at the age of 59, reportedly after a
articles.body: Sanjay Gupta, the filmmaker who gave audiences 'Kaante', 'Kaabil' and 'Shootout at Wadala', passed away on October 30 at the age of 59, reportedly after a fall in the bathroom of his Mumbai home. His passing has sent shockwaves through the industry, with tributes flowing in from colleagues, friends and fans. Among them is Amitabh Bachchan, who turned to his blog to share his grief and remember a man whose stylish, high-octane films left a lasting mark on Hindi cinema.Amitabh Bachchan’s blog post on Sanjay Gupta’s demiseReacting to the filmmaker’s death, Amitabh shared a heartfelt post on his blog on Sunday. Writing in Hindi, the veteran actor said, “A friend, a fellow artiste and a true devotee of art has left us at such a young age! I am unable to understand how all of this is happening. Our dear companions from the world of art are being snatched away from us. What wrong have they done to deserve such a fate? People say that all the powerful planets in the solar system have turned unfavourable at the same time.”He added, “Please have mercy on us! Those who are raining their wrath upon us – is this really fair? May all the planets in the solar system retreat to their respective homes and stay apart from one another. Perhaps then they will stop troubling all of us!".Sanjay Gupta’s ‘Kaante’ connection with BachchanBachchan collaborated with Sanjay on 'Kaante', a film that also starred Sanjay Dutt, Suniel Shetty, Lucky Ali, Mahesh Manjrekar and Kumar Gaurav in key roles. Dutt and Shetty have also shared emotional posts on social media remembering the filmmaker, and fans have responded with an outpouring of love and support.Sanjay Gupta’s journey from post-production to directorIn recent years, Sanjay directed 'The Miranda Brothers' (2024), starring Meezaan Jafri and Harshvardhan Rane, and 'Visfot' (2024), with Riteish Deshmukh and Fardeen Khan in the lead roles. His journey in cinema began behind the scenes: he worked in post-production and sound design, and assisted filmmaker Pankaj Parashar on projects such as the TV series 'Karamchand' and the film 'Jalwa'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar in 'Drishyam 3', the latest chapter in the Hindi crime thriller franchise.
articles.body: Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar in 'Drishyam 3', the latest chapter in the Hindi crime thriller franchise. The film arrived in theatres on October 2, 2026, bringing another chapter in Vijay's attempts to protect his family from a criminal investigation. This time, he faces a new police officer who believes he has found a way to break through the family's carefully maintained defense. While the movie continues its theatrical run, viewers are also waiting for details about its digital premiere.'Drishyam 3' OTT release: When and where to watch Ajay Devgn's film?A report by Digit.in has indicated that Netflix could stream 'Drishyam 3' between mid and late November 2026. The platform is reportedly expected to be its digital destination. However an official announcement is still awaited.'Drishyam 3': Jaideep Ahlawat enters as a determined police officerThe latest story introduces Rajveer Tomar, played by Jaideep Ahlawat. He arrives with a specific objective: to bring Vijay Salgaonkar to justice. Rajveer believes his investigation has uncovered evidence that could finally expose the weaknesses in Vijay's defense.His approach differs from that of the officers who previously tried to solve the case. Rajveer is convinced that the system must command fear and makes his position clear with the line, “System ka darr bana rehna chahiye.” His arrival puts Vijay's ability to stay ahead of the investigation under fresh pressure.Ajay Devgn returns as Vijay Salgaonkar in 'Drishyam 3'Ajay Devgn reprises his role as Vijay Salgaonkar, a man who has repeatedly managed to protect his family despite police scrutiny. His character has become central to the franchise's appeal because audiences are made to support someone whose actions raise moral questions.Even as Rajveer believes he has the evidence to corner him, Vijay remains confident about his ability to handle the situation. articles.title: How one Shrewsbury musician turned disability and isolation into a song
articles.summary: Nikki Rous says music has become a way of processing the challenges of disability and illness.
articles.body:
When people talk about disability, the conversation often focuses on symptoms, treatment and physical barriers.

Less often discussed is the loneliness that can accompany chronic illness and disability.

For singer-songwriter Nikki Rous, a wheelchair user, that experience became the inspiration for a new song exploring the isolation that can accompany disability and chronic illness.

"I think as a disabled person, and [with] many other people that suffer from chronic illness, chronic pain and disability, there's a certain amount of isolation," she said.

"It's a very different lifestyle to when I was able-bodied.

"I just wanted to get that point across really about the loneliness and isolation and hopefully make some people feel not so alone."

Her latest song, No Space Left, draws on personal experience, but touches on feelings that many people living with long-term health conditions may recognise.

For Rous, songwriting has become a way of processing experiences that can be difficult to explain.

"It's quite cathartic for me," she said.

"If I'm having a tough time, I'll generally write it all out, produce a song and then I've kind of moved on from that place."

The song is informed in part by her experience of living with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) , a group of rare inherited conditions that affect the body's connective tissues.

Connective tissue supports the skin, joints, blood vessels and organs, and symptoms can include chronic pain, fatigue and mobility problems.

Rous said EDS was the condition she was born with, although she also lives with other related conditions.

"It's a genetic connective tissue disorder that affects your collagen production and the connective tissue throughout your whole body, so it causes multisystemic problems," she said.

Although disability is rarely a subject heard in chart music, she believes there is value in writing openly about experiences that are often overlooked.

Asked whether that was part of her motivation, she replied: "Yes, I think so.

"Maybe part of that reason is because we're too ill to get to that level. The touring, the recording and everything that goes with it."

Her songs have long explored difficult subjects, including mental health and heartache, and she said audience members frequently tell her they recognise their own experiences in her lyrics.

"I did get a lot of people coming up to me after gigs and saying that they felt really seen and heard," she said.

"They've not really spoken openly about things that were affecting them, and they can see that someone else is able to do that."

Music has been at the centre of her life since childhood. Originally hailing from Tamworth, but now based in Shropshire, Rous has supported acts including Level 42 and Jamiroquai during her career, while continuing to write and perform original material.

Away from the stage, she has also spent the past eight years helping other artists find an audience through a songwriter showcase she runs at Albert's Shed in Shrewsbury.

But since undergoing spinal surgery in 2019, she said both her mobility and pain levels have worsened, making some aspects of performing increasingly difficult.

"It might be getting to the point where I will no longer be able to play music," she said.

"It's getting harder to play guitar. My voice, obviously, that's full of connective tissue, your vocal cords, so it's not what it used to be."

Despite that uncertainty, she remains determined to continue writing and performing for as long as possible.

"It's really just to get all these ideas out that I never recorded," she said.

"I will continue gigging [for] as long as I can."

For Rous, No Space Left is an attempt to shine a light on an experience that often goes unspoken. Through her music, she hopes people living with disability, chronic illness and isolation will feel, as she puts it, "not so alone".

articles.title: Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything,’ ‘Clayface’ lead sleepy Halloween weekend
articles.summary: The North American box office took a bit of a hit this weekend with the Halloween holiday drawing audiences away from theaters on Saturday.
articles.body: The North American box office took a bit of a hit this weekend with the Halloween holiday drawing audiences away from theaters on Saturday. Ticket sales were led by the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” and the DC Studios movie “Clayface,” and aren’t likely to surpass $56 million, according to studio estimates on Sunday. That would make it the second-lowest-earning weekend of the year. “You Can See Everything” had the slight edge over “Clayface,” with $10.6 million from 2,655 locations in its third weekend in theaters. The Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim-directed film has made $63.9 million to date against a reported production budget of $7 million and continues to generate the kind of buzz that’s hard to buy. This is the first time it’s hit No. 1, however. “Clayface,” about the Batman villain, trailed “You Can See Everything” by only $200,684. The Warner Bros. release fell 57% in its second weekend in theaters. That brings its domestic earnings to $44.1 million against a reported $44 million budget. Third place went to Laika’s animated film “Wildwood,” which added 150 screens in its second weekend, bringing its footprint to 3,100 theaters in the U.S. and Canada. The Fathom Entertainment release made an estimated $7.5 million, down 39% from its first weekend, bringing its running total to $25.9 million. The comedic fantasy “Wicker,” in which Olivia Colman plays a woman who commissions a basket maker to build her a wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgård), landed in fourth place with $4.1 million. “Street Fighter,” now in its third weekend, rounded out the top five with $3.2 million. In notable expansions, the acclaimed Sundance indie “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York” added over 1,000 locations in its second weekend and made $1.9 million, which landed it in the top 10. Netflix also reported earnings from the theatrical release of its World War II film “The Mosquito Bowl,” which made $455,000 from 349 locations. “La Bola Negra” made slightly less, $418,000, from only 38 locations in its third weekend, bringing its running total to $1.2 million. The domestic box office remains up over 17% from last year with nearly $8.5 billion to date. Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “You Can See Everything,” $10.6 million. 2. “Clayface,” $10.4 million. 3. “Wildwood,” $7.5 million. 4. “Wicker,” $4.1 million. 5. “Street Fighter,” $3.2 million. 6. “Resident Evil,” $2.5 million. 7. “Other Mommy,” $2.5 million. 8. “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” $1.9 million. 9. “Heart of the Beast,” $1.6 million. 10. “Sense and Sensibility,” $1.4 million.

articles.title: 'Hanuman Ansh' makers issue warning over film's rights after its Rs 342 crore box-office run: 'All rights only through the process set out in the inter-se agreements'
articles.summary: The makers of 'Hanuman Ansh' have issued a clarification regarding the film's ownership, rights and official representation, stating that no individual
articles.body: The makers of 'Hanuman Ansh' have issued a clarification regarding the film's ownership, rights and official representation, stating that no individual can independently claim authority to handle its affairs. Swambhu Media Network Pvt. Ltd. has emphasised that all decisions concerning the film must be taken in accordance with agreements signed between its producers. The statement also cautions against unauthorised transactions, public claims or commitments made using the film's name.Based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba, popularly known as Maharaj ji, 'Hanuman Ansh' has four officially recognised producers: Namrata G Singh, Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi, Ragini Sona and Anupriya Nagar. The production company has clarified that all rights associated with the project, including theatrical, OTT, television, music, gaming and licensing rights across India and international markets, are governed by agreements between these producers.The company has further stated that matters concerning the film's publicity, award nominations, commercial rights and business collaborations cannot be handled independently. Such decisions require the producers' approval and must be routed through the company's authorised channels. It has also made it clear that any agreements, public announcements or award-related claims made without the necessary consent will not be considered valid or binding.The statement read, “The Company is aware that an individual is representing themselves as authorised to deal with the rights in the Film. No individual holds that authority. All rights in the Film (theatrical, streaming, broadcast, music, gaming, licensing, etc.), in India and Internationally, are dealt with only through the process set out in the inter-se agreements executed amongst the Producers.”As part of the clarification, the production house has designated Namrata G Singh and Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi as the film's sole Executive Directors. They will be responsible for overseeing public relations, marketing, awards and strategic partnerships, ensuring that all official communication and decisions are handled through a single authorised team.The makers have also issued guidelines for the film's cast and crew, stating that they must obtain prior approval before participating in any public engagement related to the project. This includes media interviews, podcasts, YouTube shows and other promotional appearances. Those interested in such engagements have been asked to contact the authorised representatives and secure formal confirmation beforehand.Reiterating its position, the company stated, “No party acting alone has authority to deal in the Film. Any such dealing is invalid and not binding on the Company or the Producers. Any statement, award claim or business arrangement made outside this process is not recognised by the Company. Those who engage outside it do so entirely at their own risk.”Explaining the need to safeguard the film's identity and association with Maharaj ji, Executive Directors Namrata G Singh and Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi said, “Hanuman Ansh belongs to Maharaj ji’s devotees across the world. Our duty is to protect it, and to give every partner one clear and verified door to the Film.”Swambhu Media Network has also warned that it will pursue appropriate action across territories against anyone attempting to misuse the film's name, credits or intellectual property.The clarification comes after 'Hanuman Ansh' reportedly registered an impressive theatrical run at the box office. Made on a reported budget of Rs 2 crore, the film has earned Rs 342.44 crore in net collections in India and Rs 452.86 crore worldwide, according to figures shared by Sacnilk. These figures account for its 87-day theatrical run. Written and directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, the film is based on his book 'Divine Detour: That Changed My Life'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Heidi Klum's Halloween costume may have exposed secrets about 'The Batman Part II'
articles.summary: Fans spotted possible clues about the movie's villains in a post showing how Klum's severed-hand Halloween costume was made.
articles.body:
Clues about the villains in Robert Pattinson's upcoming Batman sequel may have been accidentally revealed in an Instagram post about Heidi Klum's Halloween costume.

The supermodel dressed as a giant, gruesome severed hand for Halloween, complete with replicas of her wedding rings — and a behind-the-scenes post showing the costume's creation appears to reveal objects linked to several Batman villains.

Eagle-eyed social media users spotted the items in what is reportedly the workspace of special effects makeup artist Mike Marino, who created Klum's costume and previously worked on 2022's The Batman and its HBO spinoff, The Penguin .

Among the objects visible was a facial cast that fans said resembled actor Brian Tyree Henry with a disfigured lip. Some connected it to Two-Face, a Batman villain who was once Gotham City's district attorney, Harvey Dent, before an attack left half his face disfigured.

The image also showed a box labeled "Zsasz." Victor Zsasz is the name of a serial killer from the comics who carves tally marks into his skin for each person he kills.

The post has renewed speculation about Sebastian Stan's role in the upcoming film. In June, entertainment journalist Jeff Sneider reported that Stan would play Zsasz in The Batman Part II , while Henry would portray Harvey Dent / Two-Face. Neither casting claim has been officially confirmed.

Another box was labeled "Owl 3," which fans have speculated could refer to the Court of Owls, a secret society that influences Gotham City in DC Comics.

Marino confirmed his involvement in The Batman Part II in an October interview with W magazine , adding to speculation that the objects could be connected to the sequel. "To be honest, I'm a comic book nerd, so the fact that I'm working on [ The Batman: Part II ] is a dream scenario," he said. "We're doing some really cool makeup in this new movie, so that's the dream right there."

However, none of the apparent clues have been confirmed to belong to the new movie, and there is no indication that the objects were deliberately included in the Halloween post as hints about it. Yahoo has contracted Marino for comment.

Director Matt Reeves confirmed Henry and Stan's involvement in the sequel in May but did not reveal which characters they would play. Variety said Stan was "set to play" Harvey Dent.

Stan told the Happy Sad Confused podcast in an episode released in October that the movie is "going to be great," adding, "This is definitely, for me, feeling like something very different than I've gotten to do. And that's what I love, and I'm excited about."

The Batman Part II is scheduled to hit theaters on Feb. 18, 2028. It was originally due for release in October 2025 but was delayed by the Hollywood strikes.

Production was temporarily halted last month as Reeves stepped away for personal reasons . Ocean's Eleven director Steven Soderbergh was hired to help finish filming. The original movie was released in March 2022.

articles.title: Imran Khan apologises as Bombay High Court slams the actor for participating in protests despite being an OCI card holder: 'If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated?'
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court on Monday pulled up actor Imran Khan, a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, for participating in a protest
articles.body: The Bombay High Court on Monday pulled up actor Imran Khan, a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, for participating in a protest related to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) issue in Mumbai. The court observed that the fundamental right to protest is reserved for Indian citizens, following which the actor tendered an unconditional apology and assured the bench that he would not participate in any such demonstration in the future.A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna observed that India's magnanimity was evident from the fact that Khan, despite being a US citizen, was first served a notice asking him to leave the country rather than being deported immediately.Appearing for Khan, senior advocate Venkatesh Dhond promptly submitted an undertaking on behalf of the 43-year-old actor, assuring the court that he would neither participate in protests in the future nor encourage anyone else to do so. He also tendered an unconditional apology.The court subsequently scheduled Khan's petition challenging the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) notice for further hearing on December 7. The notice had directed him to leave India by October 28 over his alleged participation in a demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Mumbai last month. The bench also extended its earlier order keeping the FRRO notice in abeyance until the next hearing.During the proceedings, the court maintained that an OCI cardholder does not enjoy the same rights as an Indian citizen, particularly when it comes to participating in protests. Drawing a comparison with how foreign nationals are treated in other countries, the bench remarked, "If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated? If this had happened in America, the person would have been put on the next flight back to India,"The judges also suggested that Khan consider applying for Indian citizenship if he wished to participate in demonstrations concerning issues affecting Indian citizens. While the bench acknowledged that the authorities were within their sovereign powers to issue the notice, it also urged them to consider the circumstances before taking further action."He (Khan) is ready to tender an unconditional apology. He has been in India since childhood. Show some magnanimity and a big heart now. We have to be 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family)," the court observed.At the same time, the judges made it clear that the actor could not take his OCI status for granted. Referring to the powers available to the government under the law, the bench said, "As an OCI cardholder, you (Khan) are at the mercy of this country. Hence, such behaviour cannot be tolerated, but one chance can be given," the HC said. The court also questioned Khan's reason for attending a demonstration concerning an issue linked to Indian electoral processes. Asking what connection the actor had with the SIR exercise, the bench remarked that he had no right to participate in a protest concerning Indian citizens."For what had he (Khan) gone to a place of protest (in Mumbai)?" the judges asked, adding in a lighter vein that the actor did not even have an upcoming film to promote. "The rights Indian citizens enjoy and the rights available to OCI cardholders are different. If he had been an Indian citizen then the situation would have been different," Chief Justice Tripathi noted.Reiterating its position, the bench added that Khan's OCI status did not entitle him to exercise the same privileges as an Indian citizen. "You (Khan) had no right to participate in a protest of such nature. You have no connection with the SIR (Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls undertaken by EC). The right to protest is not available to an OCI cardholder," the HC said.The judges further took note of Khan's social media activity following his release from police detention, observing that his posts could influence his young followers."Your social media posts (after he was released from detention by police) amounted to instigation. You have young followers who are bound to get influenced," the court said.The FRRO issued the 'Leave India' notice under Sections 7(2)(C) and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, provisions that empower the government to regulate the movement of foreign nationals and order their removal from the country. Khan was directed to leave India by October 28, failing which deportation proceedings could be initiated.The action followed his brief detention by Mumbai Police during a demonstration held on October 10 at the city's historic August Kranti Maidan. The protest was organised in solidarity with an agitation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which had demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls.In his petition challenging the FRRO's decision, filed through advocate Zulfiquar Memon, Khan maintained that he had neither participated in the gathering nor had any association or affiliation with its organisers.Describing the notice as "illegal, arbitrary, perverse and drastic," the actor alleged that the authorities had failed to apply their minds before targeting him because of his public profile. articles.title: Years before making Rs 400 crore 'Ramayana', Namit Malhotra mortgaged house to invest Rs 7 lakh into VFX business, took Rs 2 crore loan from bank: 'We would have become homeless'
articles.summary: Ever since Ranbir Kapoor-starrer 'Ramayana' was announced, producer Namit Malhotra has been at the centre of curiosity, with many wondering about the man
articles.body: Ever since Ranbir Kapoor-starrer 'Ramayana' was announced, producer Namit Malhotra has been at the centre of curiosity, with many wondering about the man backing one of Indian cinema's most ambitious projects, reportedly mounted on a budget of Rs 4,000 crore. A third-generation member of a film family, Namit's journey to becoming a filmmaker was far from conventional. He started his entrepreneurial journey at just 18, built a visual effects company from scratch and even saw his family home being mortgaged to keep his dream alive. His ultimate ambition was always to make a film on a scale that could compete with the best in the world.Namit's association with cinema goes back generations. His grandfather, MN Malhotra, began his career as a cameraman and went on to shoot 'Jhansi Ki Rani', regarded as the first Indian film shot in colour. His father, Naresh Malhotra, also ventured into film production and backed projects such as 'Shahenshah'. Growing up in a family immersed in filmmaking, Namit naturally developed aspirations of becoming a director.In an old interview with Komal Nahta on ETC, recorded nearly 15 years ago, Namit spoke about his early ambitions and how he eventually found his way into the world of visual effects.“I wanted to become a filmmaker. I was extremely focused growing up to become a director and make films. Around that time, my father started a new business. So it seemed like a good opportunity to fill the technological gap in our industry.”Recalling a conversation with his father when he turned 18, Namit said, “After turning 18, I was asked by my father what I wanted to do career-wise. I was not a very studious child. I didn’t enjoy studying, so I told him there are two things I don’t want to do. I don’t want to do your business, and I hate computers. Barring these two, advise me anything.”Namit later explained that he had intentionally ruled out the two career paths he thought his father might suggest, as his own interest lay in becoming a film director. However, an unexpected conversation during a flight introduced him to the possibilities of computer graphics and changed his professional trajectory.“I bumped into my father’s friend on a flight when he asked me what I wanted to do. It was during this conversation that I told him, ‘I want to become a film director, but my father wants me to take up computer graphics.’ The friend told me that computer graphics is like filmmaking. I got fascinated, but I am not good at drawing.”Intrigued by the idea, Namit enrolled in a computer graphics course, although the experience did not go quite as planned.“It was a three-month course. I believe in shortcuts. The instructor tried to teach me, but I couldn’t get interested. At the same time, there were some developments in post-production, and an opportunity came up to offer computer-based editing services.”Instead of pursuing the course further, Namit joined hands with the instructors and started a business out of a garage. The venture was established with an initial investment of around Rs 7 lakh, partly funded by his father and partly through a bank loan. Recalling those early days, he said, “None of us had any experience. I was 19, they were 21. We invested about Rs 7 lakh. My father funded some of it, and the rest was a loan from the bank.”The small garage operation gradually developed into a full-fledged studio. As the business expanded, the team rented apartments within the same building to accommodate its growing operations. By 2006, the company had established a presence across India.Namit has often credited his father for backing his ideas without questioning his ambitions. Recalling the unwavering support he received, he said, “I would only tell him, ‘I want to do this,’ and he would be like, ‘Then go do it.’ He even said, ‘I will put the house on the line, mortgage it.'”That faith came with considerable financial risk. At one point, the family home had to be mortgaged to secure funding for the business. Reflecting on the decision and the stakes involved, Namit said, “In 1997, I knew there was no bigger risk than this. My company’s turnover was Rs 75 lakh, and the loan we had taken was Rs 2 crore. I knew that if the business failed, our story would have been completely finished. After all, it was a new technology. We would have become homeless, as we had invested everything in it. I was 21. But without flinching, my father did it, maybe because I am his only son.”Apart from taking financial risks, Namit also built his company around the belief that talent and dedication mattered more than formal qualifications. He has maintained that a person's willingness to learn and passion for the craft were more important than their educational background. Citing an example from his own team, he said, “The boy who delivered chai to our team is now a core part of our team. Today, he is one of the most well-respected creative technicians in our company. He is very well-regarded in the industry.”Over the last three decades, Namit has transformed his venture into a globally recognised visual effects company, contributing to several Hollywood productions, including 'Avatar'. With eight Oscars associated with its work and achievements, the company has built a formidable reputation in the international film industry.Having spent years developing the technological expertise and resources required to execute large-scale cinematic projects, Namit is now backing his long-held ambition with 'Ramayana'. The Rs 4,000-crore epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor, marks a significant milestone in a journey that began with a teenager determined to make films, even if he had to take an unconventional route to get there.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2016, Dakota Johnson bought her first permanent Los Angeles home for $3.55 million with her ‘Fifty Shades of Grey’ earnings; decade later, the actress sold the mid-century modern house for $5.924 million after making it her own with designer updates
articles.summary: Dakota Johnson has sold the mid-century modern house in Los Angeles that she called home for a decade.
articles.body: Dakota Johnson has sold the mid-century modern house in Los Angeles that she called home for a decade. The three-bedroom property on Marmont Avenue, with its clean lines and views of the Chateau Marmont, closed for $5.924 million in June 2026 according to Mansion Global. She had bought it in 2016 for $3.55 million, with her payout from the first instalment of the ‘Fifty Shades of Grey’ trilogy, the actress told Architectural Digest. “I thought it would be healthy to have a base,” she said. “And, at the very least, have one place where you know your stuff is, as opposed to 10 places.” The sale marks the end of a chapter in a house she once described as a place to finally put down roots, and the beginning of a new one in the Hollywood Hills.A quick sale of Dakota Johnson’s house after a short listingJohnson listed the house for $6 million and it moved fast according to Realtor.com. Within days it went under contract, and the final price came in just under the asking figure at $5.924 million. The 3,210-square-foot home sits on a gated, terraced lot and had become well known for its mid-century design, large glass walls, and thoughtful updates. After nearly ten years of ownership, the sale delivered a clear gain over the original purchase price.Dakota Johnson’s house designed by Carl MastonThe house was built in 1947 by architect Carl Maston, a name associated with California modernism. It mixes timber, concrete, and wood-framed glass in the classic mid-century style. Three matching wooden doors mark the front, and a sliding door opens straight to the swimming pool. The terraced grounds include gardens, lawns, and an outdoor fire pit, giving the place a quiet, tree-house feel even though it sits above the Sunset Strip.Pierce & Ward’s soft updates on Dakota Johnson’s residenceJohnson brought in the design firm Pierce & Ward to refresh the interiors. The kitchen became a talking point after she showed the house to Architectural Digest. In the primary suite they created a custom pink bathroom inspired by a sweater from The Row. Glass walls open the rooms to the backyard and pool, keeping the indoor-outdoor flow that defines the original architecture while adding a warmer, more personal layer.From first permanent home to a new chapterWhen Johnson bought the house in 2016, she was clear about her reason. “I wanted a place to put all my stuff,” she told Architectural Digest at the time. It was her first real base after years of moving around. Before the sale she had already moved into a different property in the Outpost Estates area of the Hollywood Hills, a Mediterranean-style house she purchased for about $5.3 million, she talked about it in an interview with Vogue. She has spoken about loving the views of olive trees and sky there, and the sense of privacy it offers “With my job and the velocity at which my schedule can change, it’s important for me to have a place to go to and it be mine,” she says. “Psychologically, I’m moored somewhere. This place is my anchor”, she said.About Dakota JohnsonDakota Johnson is an American actress who first became widely known for the ‘Fifty Shades’ films and has since built a varied career across independent and studio projects. The daughter of actors Melanie Griffith and Don Johnson, she has appeared in films such as ‘The Lost Daughter’, ‘Persuasion’, and ‘Materialists’, earning praise for her understated style and range. Off-screen she has shown a clear interest in design and quiet, personal spaces, moving from her longtime mid-century house into a new chapter in the Hollywood Hills.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: Jack Lowden says James Bond speculation is 'flattering'
articles.summary: The Slow Horses star is among three actors reported to be in the running for the iconic movie role.
articles.body:
Slow Horses star Jack Lowden has described the speculation he could be the next James Bond as "flattering".

The 36-year-old - who grew up in Oxton in the Scottish Borders - has been reported to be in the running for the role alongside Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor.

The actor chosen will replace Daniel Craig, who took over the role of Bond with Casino Royale in 2006 and bowed out after his fifth film, No Time To Die, in 2021.

Speaking to GQ Hype , Lowden responded to the rumours - but did not confirm or deny whether he was part of the auditioning process.

Jack Lowden makes appearance in old school's show

"On this… it's all very flattering," he said.

"It's nice to be mentioned – for any role – and I'm just not really going to add to the noise," he said.

Last month, his Slow Horses co-star Gary Oldman claimed the new Bond had been chosen, adding that he had his "fingers crossed" for Lowden.

Speaking to Canada's Global, Oldman said: "It's been rumoured that he's on the shortlist.

"We're going to find out pretty soon, aren't we? Because they have picked him.

"They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack."

When asked about Oldman's comments, Lowden said: "It's very nice, and Gary's a sweetheart – it's particularly lovely, coming from someone like him.

He added: "As a young male actor, generally, the minute you're not playing a zany artist type, the minute you're in a suit, people fling it at you."

During an appearance at the Toronto International Film Festival, Oldman clarified his remarks and said he had only heard a rumour that producers had selected an actor from a shortlist, not that Lowden had been cast.

He said he did not know who had got the part but he was hoping it was his co-star.

Lowden is best known for his roles in films including Dunkirk and Mary Queen Of Scots, as well as TV roles in Slow Horses and War and Peace.

The actor has also been awarded two Baftas and a Laurence Olivier Award as well as nominations for two Primetime Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe Award.

He is next starring alongside Emma Corrin in Dolly Alderton's adaptation of Pride And Prejudice.

The next Bond film is in development after it was announced last year that Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight would write the script.

Amy Pascal and David Heyman will produce the upcoming project, which is currently untitled, while Dune's Denis Villeneuve will direct.

Pascal told Deadline earlier this year that a casting announcement by the end of the year was a "good bet" but that Craig was a "hard act to follow".

articles.title: Ranchi Municipal Corporation deploys 1,200 workers for Chhath festival ghats clean-up
articles.summary: Ranchi Municipal Corporation deploys 1,200 workers and lighting teams to clean 72 Chhath ghats, with zonal monitoring, safety barricades and helpline support.
articles.body: Ranchi: More than 1,200 sanitation workers and 25 special lighting teams have been deployed across 72 ghats in run up to the Chhath festival scheduled in the second week of November, the Ranchi Municipal Corporation (RMC) said in a statement issued on Monday.“The ghats have been divided into eight zones and officials assigned to monitor preparations and address issues on the ground. Deep-water stretches at major ghats are being identified and barricaded to strengthen safety measures. Four horticulture teams have also been deployed to prune hazardous tree branches and clear obstructions near water bodies,” it read.The RMC has also intensified cleaning operations at ghats and approach roads, with workers engaged in garbage removal, sweeping, grass cutting, and bleaching powder spraying, it said.Appealing to residents to use 24x7 helpline number 1800-570-1235 for complaints, suggestions, or issues related to Chhath arrangements, the civic body stated, “Mechanised cleaning is also under way at several locations. Weed-harvesting machines have been deployed at Dhurwa Dam, while poclain machines are carrying out desilting work at Swarnarekha Ghat in Namkum. Additional equipment has been pressed into service at other water bodies to expedite preparations.”The electricity wing of the RMC has also launched a drive to repair faulty streetlights and provide additional illumination at ghats and adjoining routes.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: 'Homestead' star Bailey Chase says California vaccine plans were 'final straw' that drove family out of LA
articles.summary: Bailey Chase reveals the proposed COVID-19 vaccine mandate that drove his family from California to the mountains of North Carolina five years ago.
articles.body: "Homestead" star Bailey Chase is opening up about the "final straw" that drove him and his family out of California for a new life in North Carolina. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 54-year-old actor, who shares daughter Waverly, 12, and 10-year-old twins Maggie and Gauge with his wife Amy, explained that concerns over how California's COVID-19 restrictions would impact his children led him to leave the Golden State behind. "That happened five years ago in the throes of COVID," Chase said. "My wife and I picked up sticks with our three young children when they were mandating vaccines out there." "They said they couldn't go back to school without it," Chase, who stars as former Green Beret Jeff Eriksson in "Homestead," continued. "And that was the final straw. And we've been in the mountains of North Carolina ever since living our best life." ZACHARY LEVI SAYS TEXAS GIVES HIM THE ‘FREEDOM’ HE COULDN’T FIND IN CALIFORNIA Five years after trading Los Angeles for North Carolina, Chase told Fox News Digital that his life now largely revolves around his children's activities when he isn't working. 'VIRGIN RIVER' STAR BEN HOLLINGSWORTH SAYS HIS KIDS HAVE FREEDOM IN SMALL TOWN THAT 'DOESN'T FLY' IN LA "I'm like soccer dad right now. It's soccer season, so we're going here and there," he said. "My oldest is really into ballet, and I couldn't be more proud of her and getting ready for ‘The Nutcracker’ in December, and basketball season's around the corner." While Chase remains committed to his acting career, the "Longmire" alum said his priorities shift completely when he returns home. CHRIS PRATT SAYS HIS FAITH WILL BE 'THE MOST IMPORTANT THING' THAT HE PASSES ON TO HIS KIDS "I love my job, and when I'm off filming, I'm 100% focused on that. But when I'm home, I'm home," he said. "There's no greater job than being a dad." Chase and his family currently live in Amy's hometown of Hendersonville in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Western North Carolina, about 25 miles south of Asheville. Chase has previously explained that Amy had long envisioned eventually returning to the area where she was born and raised. The actor also has ties to North Carolina after attending Duke University in Durham on a football scholarship. 'RANSOM CANYON' STAR JOSH DUHAMEL SAYS HE'D RATHER PUT MONEY INTO NORTH DAKOTA AFTER SELLING LOS ANGELES HOME "Amy, being from the mountains of North Carolina, always had it in the back of her mind that she’d go back home one day," he said in a January 2026 interview with Duke Alumni Magazine. "We didn’t know how or when." However, Chase recalled they decided the time was right due to California's handling of the pandemic. ‘TWILIGHT’ STAR KELLAN LUTZ TRADED CALIFORNIA FOR TENNESSEE LAND AND BIBLE STUDIES "Things started to not work in LA during COVID – they shut down the schools, there were no sports for the kids," he said. "Really, no life, no work. And it became more and more obvious that we should leave LA." "Amy’s very close with her parents, who are in N.C.," he continued. "Everything’s about seven minutes away: school, the in-laws, the grocery store, golf course, soccer field. It’s a great location. We live in a house that would not have been affordable in LA." JANA KRAMER SAYS LOS ANGELES PRICED HER OUT OF THE CHILDHOOD SHE WANTED FOR HER KIDS "It’s a kid’s dream," he added. "There’s a sports court and a pool. We have two golden retriever puppies, so it’s a full and lively house." During a February appearance on the "Undaunted.Life: A Man's Podcast," Chase elaborated on the concerns that he had over California's proposed vaccine mandate for his young children's return to school. "At that time, you know, they're 4, 4 and 6 years old," he recalled. "I got two young girls and, you know we don't need to go down that rabbit hole." "I was like, 'No, I just don't know enough,'" he continued. "And I got one job right now, and it's to take care of these little nuggets. That's the most important job I have right now." In October 2021, California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced plans for a COVID-19 vaccine requirement for students that he said would eventually apply to all the state's 6.7 million public and private schoolchildren. However, the mandate was repeatedly delayed and ultimately never took effect. In February 2023, state health officials announced that they would not pursue or implement the requirement as the COVID-19 state of emergency expired at the end of that month. 'ANT-MAN' STAR EVANGELINE LILLY SAYS SHE LEFT HOLLYWOOD BECAUSE SHE 'ALWAYS HATED BEING FAMOUS' Chase previously acknowledged that while relocating to North Carolina was the best move for his family, leaving LA came at a professional cost after he spent 21 years building his career in Hollywood. "I've lost out on some work by not being in L.A.," he admitted while appearing on the "Living Local" podcast in August. "There was a big role on 'Grey's Anatomy,'" he continued. "And I understand, it's a lot cheaper for them. They just move on to the next guy and cast someone who's local to L.A." "But what has happened is I've gotten new opportunities and different kind of jobs and some faith-based films and shows," Chase added. The "Saving Grace" actor has also spoken openly about how he "lost touch" with God during his years in LA and shared that moving to North Carolina eventually led him back to his Christian faith. "Moving back here, I've gotten reconnected to my faith," Chase told "Crosswalk" in January. "Just started going to church recently. It took a few years, but I really like the church where we're going to here." "My cousin started taking us," he continued. "The girls are in youth group. They really love it." "It's nice to be in an environment where I can openly talk about God and Jesus and without fear of criticism," he added. WATCH HERE: ‘HOMESTEAD’ STAR BAILEY CHASE SAYS CALIFORNIA VACCINE PLANS WERE ‘FINAL STRAW’ THAT DROVE FAMILY OUT OF LA In a 2024 Instagram post, Chase reflected on how his priorities have shifted since leaving behind "all that worry, all that stress, 20 years of hustle in LA." "It also got me thinking if I spent as much time chasing God as I’ve spent chasing success the last 25 years, what would that look like?" he wrote. Chase is currently starring as former Green Beret Jeff Eriksson in the faith-based streaming platform Angel Studios’ post-apocalyptic drama "Homestead," which will premiere its second season on Nov. 3. The series follows survivors living at a fortified prepper compound in the Rocky Mountains known as The Homestead after a nuclear attack on LA plunges the country into chaos. After the bomb is detonated, Jeff escapes with his family to The Homestead, where he serves as head of security. The actor starred in the 2024 theatrical movie "Homestead," which introduces the story and the TV series picks up directly afterward. The cast also includes Neal McDonough, Kevin Lawson Emmanuel McCord, Jesse Hutch, Betzaida Landín, Charles Esten and Dawn Olivieri. "'Homestead' has changed all of our lives and the first thing I did when I came home after the film was arm my home more," he said. "And then right before season two, Hurricane Helene hit here in the mountains of North Carolina. And I now have a brand-new generator and some other things." When asked if most Americans would be able to survive a major disaster, Chase predicted that it would be more challenging for people who live in bigger cities. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "And how that translates to me being an actor, that's why I'm so proud of ‘Homestead’ and the story that we get to tell, because it reflects my own personal values," he continued.
